title: Claire Castro downplays playing of 'Anak' for Marcos in China
summary: SHENZHEN, China -- Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro downplayed the playing of the late folk singer-songwriter Freddie Aguilar"s composition “Anak” to welcome President Ferdinand “Bongbong”…

blocks.text: SHENZHEN, China — Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro downplayed the playing of the late folk singer-songwriter Freddie Aguilar’s composition “Anak” to welcome President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. in China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.
According to Castro, Filipinos should be proud of the classic song as it has been translated into various languages.
“Ang kantang "Anak" ni Freddie Aguilar ay isa sa pinakatumatak na awit sa buong mundo. Internationally recognized at ipinagmamalaki natin ang awitin na ‘yan,” the Palace official said.
(The song Anak by Freddie Aguilar is one of the most iconic songs worldwide. It is internationally recognized, and we take great pride in it.)
“Isang classic song ang "Anak". Dapat natin itong ipagmalaki na hanggang ngayon ay sikat pa rin ang awiting ito,” she added.
(Anak is a true classic. We should be proud that this song remains popular even up to now.)

An orchestra in Shenzhen, China played an instrumental version of the Filipino song when Marcos and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos entered a hall in Shenzhen on Wednesday for a gala dinner with fellow leaders.
Released in 1978, Anak talks about a child who rebelled against his/her parents and fell into bad habits. — BAP, GMA News
